doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: SuperSax and knowing when to retire
summary: Recording with SuperSax; Ray Brown on when to quit; Hanna cannot keep up the fast tempos.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Oh, man, you played with SuperSax?

Yeah, SuperSax, that’s right. I was with them. I made a couple of albums with them. Three or four albums. They called me to come back and do another one. They had Lawrence Morro who was a very good drummer, but they were doing fast tunes and Lawrence was not quite up to that stuff. And they had to add trumpets, voices, a big orchestra, plus the SuperSax. Plus they’re doing the old things see? And Don Lamond called me up one day and he says — no Ray Brown. Ray Brown call me up and he says, “Gee, how do you know when you’ve had it, when to get off?” Like a fighter. He never knows when he’s had it and they always quit too late. He says, “How do you know that in our business, Jake?” I says, “Gee I don’t know, I’m not ready to get through yet.” Well they did these old tunes they’d done on the original records, we had to do some of them. I started repeating myself, I couldn’t get anymore new things going. And I called Ray the next day and I says, “I think it’s time for me to get off this stuff.” Then I explained to him what we did, we did some old stuff. Re-did some old stuff, and man I couldn’t make it at all. Couldn’t hear it you know. I think it’s time for me to get off. Time to retire. He says, “Yeah I do the same thing, I have a lot of trouble with that stuff. Stuff I could do years ago” he says, “I can’t do anymore.” I listened to a thing the other day, my wife played an old record “Hell Don’t Your Apple Honey” we did live and it’s [scats] about that tempo you know. And I played that on four-four when I played on that band, with 16 guys. And man I didn’t get through eight bars of that thing.
I’ve got to start practicing you know.
